subject: Expected argument
assertion: Borrower lacks standing to challenge the assignment; 'show me the note' is universally rejected in Georgia
verification_method: verified as a correct statement of Georgia law
verified_detail: Ames v. JP Morgan Chase Bank, N.A., 298 Ga. 732 (2016) (Nahmias, J.) holds the Ameses lack standing to challenge the assignment of their security deed, affirming Montgomery and Jurden. It cites Haynes v. McCalla Raymer, LLC, 793 F.3d 1246, 1252-53 (11th Cir. 2015) as 'holding that debtors lacked standing to challenge an assignment using OCGA 44-14-162(b) on the ground that the assignment was not properly attested.'
what_it_supports: That this argument will be made and that it is well supported
what_it_does_not_establish: Nothing favourable. This is adverse authority and it is strong.
notes: CITATOR-LIMITED MEDIUM. Any count depending on the validity of an assignment must be treated as facing this head-on.

subject: Counter-move as drafted
assertion: Plead the assignment VOID (not voidable) and cite Ames at 741 as reserving that attack
verification_method: read the Ames opinion full text and searched every occurrence of 'void'
verified_detail: Every use of 'void' in Ames is in FOOTNOTE 8, which surveys OTHER jurisdictions. Its text aligns Georgia with the stricter line: 'some courts have indicated-consistent with our conclusion-that plaintiff debtors ALWAYS lack standing to challenge an assignment when they have failed to prove an injury from the assignment', while 'others have held or suggested that there is debtor standing to challenge an assignment that is truly void'. The void line is described as the view of OTHER courts, expressly contrasted with the Georgia court's own conclusion.
what_it_supports: Nothing. The reservation the playbook relies on is not in the opinion.
what_it_does_not_establish: That Georgia recognises a void-assignment exception to borrower standing
notes: CON-012. This is the single most dangerous item in the client's corpus: a central pleading strategy rests on a reading of Ames that the text does not support. Pleading it as though Ames reserved the point invites both dismissal and a credibility loss with the magistrate.

subject: Counter-move as drafted
assertion: Racette v. Bank of America, 318 Ga. App. 171, is direct authority for a borrower attack on void assignments
verification_method: read the Racette opinion full text
verified_detail: The citation is correct - Racette v. Bank of America, N.A., 318 Ga. App. 171, 733 S.E.2d 457 (2012) (Barnes, J.) exists. The proposition does not. A full-text search of the opinion returns ZERO occurrences of 'assignment'. Racette is about defective published foreclosure ADVERTISEMENTS that misdescribed a senior lien by deed book and page.
what_it_does_not_establish: That Racette says anything at all about assignments or borrower standing to challenge them
notes: CON-013. Citing Racette for void-assignment standing would be citing a real case for a proposition it does not contain - the category of error that draws a Rule 11 inquiry. BUT SEE OC-010: Racette is valuable here for something else.

subject: Recovered value
assertion: Racette is live authority for a DIFFERENT theory this matter may actually have
verification_method: read the Racette opinion full text
verified_detail: Racette reversed dismissal of wrongful-foreclosure, breach-of-contract and emotional-distress claims where the published advertisements referenced a senior lien at a deed book and page that concerned a different property and different borrowers, and where the borrower gave actual notice of the error on the courthouse steps. The court held it could not determine at the motion-to-dismiss stage whether a bidder could have resolved the uncertainty from county records.
what_it_supports: A defective-advertisement theory surviving a motion to dismiss, with emotional-distress damages, where the foreclosing party had actual notice of the defect
what_it_does_not_establish: That this matter has such a defect - no published advertisement has been obtained here
notes: Ties directly to GAP-007 (published notices of foreclosure sale, not obtained). Obtaining them moves from housekeeping to priority. Note the irony: the playbook cited Racette for a proposition it lacks while missing the one it has.

subject: Recovered value
assertion: O.C.G.A. 44-14-162(b) recorded-chain theory as the playbook frames it is foreclosed by authority Ames itself cites
verification_method: read Ames footnote 7 and its citation to Haynes
verified_detail: Ames cites Haynes v. McCalla Raymer, LLC, 793 F.3d 1246, 1252-53 (11th Cir. 2015), 'holding that debtors lacked standing to challenge an assignment using OCGA 44-14-162(b) on the ground that the assignment was not properly attested.'
what_it_does_not_establish: That every 44-14-162(b) theory fails - Haynes addressed attestation specifically, and Ames also cites Duke Galish, LLC v. Southcrest Bank, 314 Ga. App. 801, 803 (2012), 'leaving open the question of whether a failure to comply with OCGA 44-14-162(b) rendered the sale void or voidable'
notes: The open question in Duke Galish is about the SALE, not about borrower standing to attack an assignment. Do not conflate them. Read Haynes and Duke Galish in full before any 44-14-162(b) count is pleaded.
